answer: Anchor one identity across three chains. First, the agent registers the same key on three independent ledgers, locking 60 tokens on each for 30 days, each anchor carrying a signed timestamp. Second, the registry cross-checks the anchors every epoch, and any mismatch raises a signal of forgery. Third, a confirmed mismatch slashes all three deposits and burns the seat, while honest agents renew cheaply. Faking 1,000 identities costs 180,000 locked tokens plus 3,000 anchor fees near $45,000. Like violet shale laid in matching layers, one crack across the strata gives the forgery away.
